generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential unique integers starting at 1, never NULL; no reuse.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Copy an existing parent key; with probability 0.05 emit NULL when the column is nullable; otherwise pick a parent row uniformly. For each join column plant at least one unmatched child row: NULL when nullable, otherwise an out-of-range key (max(parent key)+1).
generic_sampling_rules.integer_quantity: Uniform integer in [0, 30] for counts; positive quantities in [1, 30]. Applies only to status.bikes_available, status.docks_available, station.dock_count.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_measure: Uniform integer within the observed min/max of the column, inclusive. Applies to weather temperature, dew point, humidity, visibility, wind, cloud_cover, wind_dir_degrees and trip.duration.
generic_sampling_rules.real_measure: Uniform real within the observed min/max, rounded to 2 decimals.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Pick from the observed value pool; with probability 0.15 emit a case-variant (upper/lower) of the chosen value.
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: Pick uniformly from the listed enum values; with probability 0.1 emit a case-variant.
generic_sampling_rules.text_date: Uniform date in the observed date range, formatted per the column's date_format; with probability 0.1 emit a near-variant year (one year off) keeping the format.
generic_sampling_rules.text_free: Pick from the observed value pool; with probability 0.1 emit a near-variant (trailing/leading space or case change).
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For every nullable column, use the compact database's observed NULL fraction for that column (schema.original_values); if that fraction is 0, plant at least one NULL row only when the column is listed in null_targets; never plant NULL in NOT NULL / primary-key columns or in station columns not listed in null_targets.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary: For each listed literal, generate rows at the literal, one step below and one step above. Coerce the literal to the column's declared type before stepping: INTEGER columns step by 1 with integer arithmetic and the returned value is always an int (if the literal is non-numeric, fall back to a numeric draw within the column's range); TEXT columns (including numeric-looking codes such as weather.zip_code) are treated as strings and the 'one step' variants are string near-variants (e.g. last digit +/-1, or case change), never int+str arithmetic. The returned value must match the column's declared type.
generic_sampling_rules.tie: For ORDER/LIMIT columns, generate at least two rows sharing the same value at the listed rank.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicate: For DISTINCT columns, generate at least two rows with the same value.
generic_sampling_rules.unmatched_join: For join columns, generate at least one child row whose FK value has no parent row (when nullable, via NULL; otherwise via an out-of-range key).

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: 13/20 units fail with TypeError("unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'int' and 'str'"). The crash originates in SpecSampler.sample_boundary (instance.py): for a numeric boundary column it does `n = int(lit)` then `return n + (step - 1)`, but for weather.zip_code the boundary literals are stored as strings ('94106','94107','94108') in BOUNDARY_NUM, and for weather.max_temperature_f the pool also mixes string literals from LIKE_VARIANTS/literal pool. When `int(lit)` succeeds on a string it returns an int, but the surrounding code path for zip_code (declared TEXT) also feeds these into a TEXT column; more directly, `_draw_num`/`sample_boundary` mixing int and str causes the TypeError. The failure is deterministic (reproducible=true) and blocks generation for the majority of instances.
issues.requested_revision: Fix SpecSampler.sample_boundary so numeric boundary stepping is type-safe: coerce the literal to the column's declared type before arithmetic, and never add an int to a str. For weather.zip_code (TEXT) treat boundary values as strings (no arithmetic); for weather.max_temperature_f (INTEGER) keep integer arithmetic. Ensure the returned value matches the column's declared type. Re-run generation and confirm n_fail == 0.

issues.evidence: Validity feedback: all 7 produced instances are invalid with reasons compact_rows_missing (7) and no_rows_added (4). writer.write_instance_sqlite is called from cli._one as `write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p)` with orig_path defaulting to None, so the compact database is never copied and the DDL is re-created empty; generated rows are then appended to an empty DB. This violates the stated writer contract ('Each instance starts as a copy of the compact database') and the preservation-of-compact-rows requirement.
issues.requested_revision: Pass the original database path through to write_instance_sqlite (e.g. add orig_path to the worker args and call write_instance_sqlite(schema, inst, p, orig_path=orig)). Verify compact rows are preserved and generated rows are appended, and that validity reports compact_rows_missing == 0.

issues.evidence: Nullable-column feedback shows many columns with NULL 0 / n or NULL shares far above the compact share: e.g. weather.max_temperature_f NULL 921/3559 (~26%), weather.max_humidity 763/3559, trip.subscription_type 152/789 (~19%), trip.zip_code 165/789 (~21%), while the spec's uncertainty note says trip.zip_code observed null ~1.1%. _apply_null_rule uses share = rng.uniform(0.05, 0.30) for every NULL_TARGETS column regardless of the compact database's actual share, and applies 5% to all other nullable columns. This does not follow the interface rule 'NULL share following the compact database's share for that column'. Also station.* columns (name, city, lat, long, dock_count, installation_date) receive NULLs even though the compact station table has no nullable columns in the schema (all station columns are NOT NULL except none declared nullable) — station.name/city/lat/long/dock_count/installation_date are declared without NOT NULL in the DDL but the compact data has no NULLs; the spec's null_targets list does not include station columns, yet _apply_null_rule plants NULLs in them.
issues.requested_revision: Derive per-column NULL share from the compact database's observed NULL fraction (schema.original_values) rather than a fixed 5–30% band, and restrict NULL planting to columns that are actually nullable in the compact data / listed in null_targets. Do not plant NULLs in station columns that have no NULLs in the compact DB unless the spec explicitly lists them. Keep at least one NULL row per genuinely nullable column.

issues.evidence: Dependency handling: fill_foreign_keys_consistently copies parent keys uniformly with replacement and never emits NULL for nullable FKs (the spec's integer_fk rule says 'with probability 0.05 emit NULL when the column is nullable'). The unmatched_join rule requires at least one child row whose FK has no parent (via NULL when nullable, otherwise out-of-range key); the program never plants an out-of-range FK for non-nullable FKs and relies only on the generic NULL rule. Also _apply_derived for trip copies start_station_name/end_station_name from station via FK, but after _apply_null_rule sets FK to NULL the name is left as the previously copied value, so name and FK can disagree (name non-NULL while FK NULL), violating the 'trip.start_station_name = station.name VIA trip.start_station_id' rule for non-NULL operands.
issues.requested_revision: Implement the integer_fk NULL probability (0.05) for nullable FKs, and plant at least one unmatched child row per join column (NULL for nullable, out-of-range key for non-nullable). After NULL planting, re-derive name columns so that when the FK is NULL the name is also NULL (or vice versa) to keep the FK→name dependency consistent under three-valued logic.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: all 20 units failed with TypeError("unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'int' and 'str'"), n_ok=0, n_instances=0. The traceback points into the sampling path. In values.py NumberSampler.sample(), when the column is INTEGER but the element pool contains string literals (e.g. from literal_pool or original_values), `v = r.choice(self.elements)` returns a str, then `v += d` (d=1) raises TypeError. This is reachable for any INTEGER column whose pool mixes strings and numbers, e.g. weather.max_temperature_f (BOUNDARY_NUM ints plus literal-pool strings) or trip.duration. The NumberSampler constructor filters elements through _num(), but SpecSampler._draw_base() calls _init_sampler with `sorted({str(v) for v in literal_pool})` (values.py _init_sampler), which stringifies all literals, so the pool passed to NumberSampler is all strings; _num() converts them, but the boundary/planted values and the `v += d` path can still mix types. Regardless of the exact column, the program crashes on every unit, so no instances are produced.
issues.requested_revision: Fix the type handling in the numeric sampling path so INTEGER columns never add an int to a str: coerce chosen elements to int/float before arithmetic (or keep the pool numeric for numeric columns), and ensure boundary/planted values for INTEGER columns are ints. Re-run generation and confirm n_ok>0, n_fail=0, and rows_added populated for all four tables.

issues.evidence: SpecSampler.sample_boundary for TEXT columns steps by case change only (correct per spec), but for INTEGER columns it does `n + (step - 1)` where `n = int(lit)`; if a boundary literal for an INTEGER column is a string that is not numeric this returns the raw literal (str) into an INTEGER column, which SQLite will store as text. For weather.max_temperature_f the boundary literals are ints, so this is fine, but the general path is fragile and interacts with the crash above.
